object_description: elongated school bar and shorter sports volume forming a courtyard
design_condition: Two volumes aligned with the surrounding development create a spacious schoolyard, connected to the surroundings by passages and clearly visible through the gap between the buildings.

positive.statement: The calm urban-planning response is convincing in its consistency from the basic approach through to the architectural formulation.

position.rationale: Broad placement represents the coherent overall building response across the two visible volumes.

positive.statement: The two volumes create a clear urban structure and external spatial hierarchy with simple means.

position.target: two volumes and external spatial hierarchy
position.rationale: The gap and contrasting volumes are clearly identifiable in plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The hall forms a prominent communication space between school and city.

position.rationale: The inter-volume passage provides the most plausible location for the communication hall.

positive.statement: The entrances and access organization provide good orientation and are operationally convenient and efficient.

position.rationale: Access is anchored along the south-facing school edge at ground level.

positive.statement: The classrooms are well proportioned and the teaching areas are organized clearly.

position.rationale: Interior classrooms are approximated within the elongated school bar.

positive.statement: The restrained material and window strategy supports a calm architectural integration.

position.rationale: The south elevation supplies the clearest calibrated facade reference.

positive.statement: The compact building and durable materials support good energy performance and resource efficiency.

position.rationale: Compact massing is directly evident from the complete plan and elevation set.

positive.statement: The project has good overall economic efficiency and low floor area and volume.

position.target: economic efficiency and low floor area and volume
position.rationale: This is an unlocated economic judgment about overall area and volume.

negative.statement: The bicycle racks in the important passage and the fragile courtyard glasshouse are questionable.

position.rationale: The central passage and courtyard gap provide the plausible anchor for both questioned features.

negative.statement: The covered sports anteroom and rear courtyard offer limited spatial and experiential quality.

position.target: covered sports anteroom and rear courtyard
position.rationale: The sports-side volume and rearward courtyard region are approximated together.

negative.statement: The access zone on the school floors is unattractive, cramped, and narrow.

position.rationale: The access zone is approximated inside the elongated school volume across its stacked floors.

negative.statement: The sports area is clearly organized but its dimensions are too tight.

position.rationale: The shorter eastern volume clearly identifies the sports-side area, though interior dimensions are unresolved.

negative.statement: The direction of the structural ribs does not follow the flow of forces.

position.rationale: Ribs are not distinguishable, so the roof surface of the school bar is used as a constrained anchor.

negative.statement: The need for ribbed ceilings is questioned for cost reasons.

position.rationale: Ceilings are interior and unresolved; the upper school volume provides the nearest surface estimate.

negative.statement: The basement combination does not provide a convincing added value between the school and sports buildings.

position.target: basement combination between school and sports buildings
position.rationale: The basement judgment is anchored at ground level within the visible inter-volume connection.

negative.statement: The project lacks a more comprehensive idea for the urban development of the district and the plot.

position.target: urban development of district and plot
position.rationale: The broader plot judgment is distributed toward the rear site edge represented around the building masses.
